radiology_report:
LUMC (Leiden)
Imaging Department
Date: 15 Dec 2024
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: PSA 8.1 ng/mL, rising trend, prior biopsy Gleason 3+3. Request for PI-RADS assessment.

FINDINGS:
Prostate volume: 47.0 mL.
T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a focal, irregular hypointense lesion in the right posterior peripheral zone, measuring approximately 12 x 9 mm. On diffusion-weighted imaging, this area shows marked restricted diffusion with corresponding low ADC values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences reveal early, intense, and rapid wash-in of contrast within the same region, confirming suspicious enhancement.
No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. No suspicious lymphadenopathy in the pelvis.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS v2.1 category 5 lesion in the right posterior peripheral zone.
PSA density: 0.14 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage: cT2a.
csPCa predicted probability 0.82094896.

previous_notes.author: Dr. S. de Vries (GP)
previous_notes.text: 28 May 2024 - Dr. S. de Vries (GP): Patient presented with elevated PSA of 4.8 ng/mL. Transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy was performed. Results returned Gleason 3+3 (ISUP GG1). Discussed findings with patient; opted for close monitoring with repeat PSA in 6 months and planned MRI. Referred to urology for second opinion on management strategy given rising PSA trend.

previous_notes.author: Dr. S. de Vries (GP)
previous_notes.text: 29 Jan 2024 - Dr. S. de Vries (GP): Routine follow-up. PSA measured at 2.9 ng/mL, showing increase from previous value of 1.7 ng/mL in Feb 2023. Patient reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms, IPSS 14. No acute complaints. Advised repeat PSA in 6 months and discussed possibility of further imaging if PSA continues to rise.

pathology_report:
Biopsy 1 (28 May 2024): Histological examination of the prostate tissue cores reveals adenocarcinoma. The Gleason score is 3+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 1. The growth pattern is described as acinar, partly also poorly formed fusing or cribriform tubules. A cribriform pattern is present. Perineural invasion is not identified. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, bilateral.

Summary: The single available biopsy demonstrates ISUP grade group 1 disease with the presence of a cribriform pattern.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 3.
